territorial_scope.description: Reaches any person who makes a companion chatbot available to a user in California.

evidence.quote: “Operator” means a person who makes a companion chatbot available to a user in the state.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Introduced bill that would add Business and Professions Code Chapter 22.6.1 on companion chatbots and children's safety. It would apply to operators that make companion chatbots available to users in California, with child-safety duties, advertising and data limits, independent audits and civil enforcement.
summary.long: Introduced bill adding Chapter 22.6.1 (Companion Chatbots: Children's Safety) to the Business and Professions Code. It covers operators that make companion chatbots available to users in California. Operators must verify user age or apply child protections to all users. On or before July 1, 2027, operators must annually assess and mitigate child safety risks, publish a child safety policy, run a crisis response protocol, set parent-controlled defaults (including ephemeral mode and time limits), give AI notices to children, restrict specified outputs, provide parental controls, and offer an incident reporting mechanism. Operators may not target advertising at children using their data or sell or share children's personal information beyond authorized uses. Operators must undergo annual independent audits, reported confidentially to the Attorney General. By January 1, 2028 the Attorney General must adopt auditor regulations, a complaint mechanism and annual public reports. Public prosecutors may seek civil penalties up to $5,000 (negligent) or $15,000 (intentional) per affected child; children or parents may sue for actual damages.

relations.target_text: California Business and Professions Code, Division 8 (adds Chapter 22.6.1, Sections 22610 to 22617)
relations.note: Adds a new chapter to an existing code; the text does not amend any existing section. The definition of 'companion chatbot' is by reference to BPC § 22601, which is not part of this text.

evidence.quote: is added to Division 8 of the Business and Professions Code

relations.target_text: California Civil Code §§ 3273.65 (definition of child sexual abuse material) and 1798.500 (Title 1.81.9, age verification)
relations.note: Section 22610(e) takes the definition of child sexual abuse material from Civil Code § 3273.65. Section 22611(a) lets an operator verify age under Civil Code Title 1.81.9 (§ 1798.500), as one of two alternatives in § 22611.

evidence.quote: Verify the age of a user pursuant to Title 1.81.9 (commencing with Section 1798.500) of Part 4 of Division 3 of the Civil Code.

relations.target_text: California Penal Code § 311 (definition of obscene matter)
relations.note: Obscene matter is defined by reference to Penal Code § 311, and that definition is used in the prohibitions in § 22612(d)(5)(C) and (D).

evidence.quote: has the meaning defined in Section 311 of the Penal Code

relations.target_text: California Constitution, Article I, Section 3 (public access to records)
relations.note: SEC. 2 is a legislative finding that the act limits public access to information under Article I, Section 3, in order to protect proprietary information of audited companies.

evidence.quote: within the meaning of Section 3 of Article I of the California Constitution

relations.target_text: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. Sec. 301 et seq.)
relations.note: Exception to the prohibition on attempting to diagnose or treat a child's health, for chatbots designed for those purposes and regulated by the FDA as a medical device.

evidence.quote: as a medical device under the federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. Sec. 301 et seq.)

relations.target_text: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), Public Law 104-191
relations.note: Cited together with the FD&C Act as a second condition of the exception in § 22612(d)(5)(B), which requires the chatbot to be designed for diagnosis or treatment and regulated under both.

evidence.quote: the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) (Public Law 104-191)

notes: Drafting issues: the last section is numbered 26617 in the text, likely meant as 22617; § 22614(c)(2) reads 'to any either of the following'; § 22612(d)(3)(D) reads '2 two hours'. Section 22601 (definition of companion chatbot), which the act relies on, is not in this text. Relations are judgements about citations only; no legal basis, repeal or transposition is stated.

thresholds.variable_text: child (natural person under 18 years of age)
thresholds.measurement: Age of the natural person using the companion chatbot; the text does not state a verification window
thresholds.consequence: A user under 18 is a 'child' whose protections under Chapter 22.6.1 apply
thresholds.conditions: Applies to companion chatbot operators making a chatbot available to a user in the state

evidence.quote: “Child” means a natural person under 18 years of age.

thresholds.variable_text: parental control to disable access for children under a stated age
thresholds.measurement: Age of the child whose account is connected to a parent's account
thresholds.consequence: Operator must provide a parental control that allows a parent to disable access for children under 16
thresholds.conditions: Part of the parental controls required for child users under § 22612(d)(6)(A)

evidence.quote: Disable access for children under 16 years of age.

thresholds.variable_text: ephemeral mode: deletion of conversational history, interaction logs and user-provided personal input after the interaction
thresholds.measurement: Time from the interaction to permanent deletion from the operator's systems
thresholds.consequence: A chatbot setting meets the definition of ephemeral mode only if data is deleted within this period; operators must default child users to ephemeral mode unless a parent consents to persistent memory
thresholds.conditions: Default setting for child users under § 22612(d)(3)(A), changeable only by a parent

evidence.quote: is permanently deleted from the operator’s systems within 48 hours after the interaction.

thresholds.variable_text: time limit per single conversation for a child user
thresholds.measurement: Length of a single conversation between a child and a companion chatbot
thresholds.consequence: Operator must limit a child's single conversation to one hour as a default setting
thresholds.conditions: Default setting for child users that can be changed only by a parent

evidence.quote: Limiting the amount of time a child can spend in a single conversation with a companion chatbot to one hour.

thresholds.variable_text: total daily time a child can spend with companion chatbots under the operator's control
thresholds.measurement: Total time per day across companion chatbots under the operator's control
thresholds.consequence: Operator must limit a child's total daily time with companion chatbots under its control to two hours as a default setting
thresholds.conditions: Default setting for child users that can be changed only by a parent

evidence.quote: Limiting the total time per day a child can spend with companion chatbots under the operator’s control to 2 two hours.
